contract.review_scope: Body-level static contract; transitive application and called-module completeness are separate.
contract.purpose: Generate a candidate numeric container identifier and update a receipt container row.
inputs_defaults: containerId nvarchar(25); required, no default. It is used both as a proposed external identifier and in comparison with numeric INTERNAL_REC_CONT_NUM.
null_and_invalid_input_behavior: Nonnumeric input can fail conversion even without a collision because the candidate variable is numeric(25) and the UPDATE key comparison is numeric. Leading zeros can be normalized away by numeric conversion.

NULL input matches no equality rows, yields NULL candidate and no matching update. A collision among nonconvertible values with no qualifying numeric maximum can also produce NULL; no fallback seed is provided for that case.

Maximum-plus-one is assigned to numeric(25), despite an intermediate cast to numeric(26); overflow can occur before the later wrap search. Literal exclusion pattern was not published; it is an explicit remaining candidate-eligibility detail.
output_shape: Collision branch emits a one-column candidate SELECT before UPDATE and another after it; noncollision branch emits only the final SELECT. Result column has no explicit alias. SET NOCOUNT ON.

ordered_branches.explanation: Count matching logistics units, parent logistics units and receipt container IDs for the supplied text.

If any match exists, derive a numeric candidate from maximum convertible values plus one across all three identifier sources, using ISNUMERIC, length at most 25, a literal exclusion pattern and TRY_CAST.
If candidate reaches the coded 25-digit ceiling, reset to one and increment until absent from all three sources. Emit candidate SELECT within the collision branch.

If no collision exists, assign the supplied text to a numeric(25) variable. Then update RECEIPT_CONTAINER.CONTAINER_ID where INTERNAL_REC_CONT_NUM equals the supplied input, and emit the final candidate.

contract.status_and_quantity_effects: Writes a receipt container identifier, not received quantity or location inventory quantity.
configuration_scope_and_precedence: No sequence object, identity allocator, configuration lookup or lock-based reservation is used by this body. It checks only the three named identifier surfaces.
error_and_return_handling: No TRY/CATCH, return code or explicit transaction. The first candidate result can be emitted before UPDATE fails; consumers must not interpret that row as proof of successful mutation.
contract.transaction_ownership: No explicit transaction, commit, rollback, savepoint, TRY/CATCH or XACT_ABORT is introduced by this body; caller/session semantics remain authoritative.
concurrency: Check/max/loop and UPDATE are separate operations without reservation locks; two callers can choose the same candidate. The name does not establish global uniqueness.
contract.trigger_behavior: No trigger on RECEIPT_CONTAINER is present among the six captured SQL triggers; constraints and caller effects still apply.
external_handoffs_and_gaps: Application caller must clarify whether the supplied value is an external container ID or internal numeric row key. No operational call was made. Other identifier namespaces, uniqueness constraints and safe concurrent allocation need review.

NO_CAPTURED_REFERENCE means none of the credited channels in this exact retained corpus identified the table. It does not establish that the table is unused, obsolete, a backup, safe to delete, or absent from external application SQL.
Dynamic SQL, runtime-selected identifiers, external callers, client-generated SQL, uncaptured jobs and historical/other database code can use tables without a resolvable reference here.

The bounded lexer recognizes named SQL relation/DML positions and local aliases/CTEs; it is not the SQL Server binder. Unqualified names assume a unique captured name, not verified caller/default-schema resolution. Unsupported or ambiguous syntax remains explicit.

Foreign keys are structural relationships and never count as procedure/function usage. View paths are catalog/source paths; attached trigger paths are possibilities, not proof the event fired.
